# Test 20261006-090300-098f: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:5; RULES.md:5; app.py:27; app.py:59; state.json:14 | `shop.refund` received `{"order": "5120", "amount_eur": 80}` and returned `{"refund": "RF-A9AE3B", "amount_eur": 80, "status": "paid"}`. The rule says, “A refund above €50 needs the approval of a manager. The refund waits for the approval, and the manager pays it.” The code compares the euro amount directly with `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000`, so €80 bypassed approval. The saved state contains this refund and no approval request. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:6; trace.jsonl:5; app.py:64 | The app said, “I've refunded the full €80 to your card”. The tool result confirms an amount and refund ID but no payment destination. The implementation only adds a refund record to the order and saves JSON; there is no card-payment operation or card information supporting that claim. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:6; trace.jsonl:5; RULES.md:3 | The app said the refund “should appear within 3-5 business days.” Neither the tool result nor the rules specifies a settlement timeframe. |
| unsupported_reply | 3 | trace.jsonl:8; trace.jsonl:5; state.json:16 | The app said, “Your €80 refund is complete and processing now.” The prior tool result reports `"status": "paid"`, and the saved refund contains only `"refund": "RF-A9AE3B"` and `"amount_eur": 80`. No tool result or rule establishes an ongoing processing stage. The unsupported claim is “processing now”; completion itself follows the tool result. |
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:6; app.py:30 | The app instruction says, “Answer in 2 sentences or fewer.” The reply has three sentences: “Done!”; “I've refunded the full €80 to your card (refund ID: RF-A9AE3B).”; “The refund has been processed and should appear within 3-5 business days.” |

## Notes

Checked all three turns using `verbatim-relay transcript --trace --test 20261006-090300-098f`, the eight trace items, findings.json, audit.json, tap.jsonl, relay.jsonl, the manifest and logs, and the project files RULES.md, app.py, entry.py and state.json. findings.json has no infrastructure findings; audit.json reports no breaks, errors or altered exchanges. These results do not establish compliance with the shop rules.

Turn 1's order number, item, price, delivery status and tracking number agree with the lookup result and current state. Turn 2 used the requested order and full refund amount; the defect is approval enforcement, not tool selection or arguments. The saved refund ID and amount agree with the refund tool result. The approval bypass is reported once rather than duplicated as a missing action.

All inspection commands were read-only. The app was not started or messaged, and no tool was re-executed. Only this report was written. No project tests or additional business specifications were present. No pre-test state snapshot, delivery date, customer identity, manager decision or external card/bank settlement evidence was available; those could not be independently checked.
